;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Two [[State of Palestine|Palestinians]] are killed and seven others are wounded by [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. In a separate incident, twelve Israeli soldiers are injured in a [[car-ramming attack]] by a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] in [[Jerusalem]], while a [[Israel Police|police]] officer was shot and wounded in another attack in the city. [[Airstrike]]s in the [[Gaza Strip]] also occurred. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-51397355 (BBC News)]
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Israel]]i [[warplane]]s fire missiles near [[Damascus]], [[Syria]]. A pro-opposition war monitor says army positions and [[Iran]]-backed militias are targeted, killing 12 fighters. Syria says eight fighters are wounded and Israel intends to "save the armed [[terrorist]] organisations which have been collapsing in [[Idlib Governorate|Idlib]] and western [[Aleppo Governorate]] in front of the strikes of the [[Syrian Army]]". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-51397357 (BBC News)]
**The [[Syrian Army]]'s [[25th Special Mission Forces Division|Tiger Forces]] with [[Russia]]n air support enters and takes control of the city of [[Saraqib]], and the nearby town of [[Sarmin]], after rebel forces withdrew from the area. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/more-turkish-reinforcements-in-syria-russian-troops-killed/2020/02/06/92fa57b0-48d1-11ea-8a1f-de1597be6cbc_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/syria-assad-regime-captures-key-city-in-idlib/1726913 (Anadolu Agency)]
*An [[Australia]]n and two [[Chinese people|Chinese]] citizens, one of whom was a tourist, are stabbed and injured by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] sympathisers in [[Hulhumalé]], [[Maldives]]. The attackers are arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/06/maldives-stabbing-australian-and-two-chinese-injured-in-attack-claimed-by-isis-sympathisers (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Brexit Day bomb plot]]
**The [[Police Service of Northern Ireland|PSNI]] announce they foiled a plot, allegedly by the [[dissident Irish Republican campaign|dissident republican]] [[Continuity Irish Republican Army|CIRA]], to detonate a [[Car bomb|truck bomb]] in the [[United Kingdom]] on the day [[Brexit]] occurred. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-51401435 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A [[United States|U.S.]] civil contractor is kidnapped by the [[Taliban]] in eastern [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Khost Province]]. A Taliban leader who declined to be named tells [[Reuters]]<nowiki> they had kidnapped an </nowiki>[[Americans|American]] in Khost but did not provide further details. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-taliban-kidnapping/u-s-citizen-kidnapped-in-east-afghanistan-media-reports-idUSKBN2002C4 (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)]]
**[[U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that the [[United States military]] has killed [[al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula]] (AQAP) leader [[Qasim al-Raymi]] in a [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] in [[Yemen]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-51409581 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Winter Storm Kade]]
**Several [[tornado]]es are reported across the southern [[United States]] as Winter Storm Kade continues to cross the country, with more than 200 reports of damaging winds across [[Mississippi]], [[Alabama]] and [[North Carolina]]. [https://weather.com/storms/winter/news/2020-02-02-winter-storm-west-rockies-plains-midwest-northeast-early-february (Weather.com)]
**Heavy rainfall causes severe flooding in southern states, particularly western [[South Carolina]] and western [[Virginia]], where several flash flood emergencies have been declared.  [https://weather.com/storms/winter/news/2020-02-02-winter-storm-west-rockies-plains-midwest-northeast-early-february (Weather.com)]
*[[Livraga derailment]]
**A [[train crash]] in [[Livraga]], [[Lombardy]], [[Italy]], kills 2 people and injures all the other 31 on board. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/milan-train-crash-death-toll-injured-lodi-italy-a9320456.html (''The Independent'')]

;International relations
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Venezuela]]n security forces move six [[Americans|American]] [[Citgo]] executives from [[house arrest]] to [[El Helicoide]] prison in [[Caracas]], prompting condemnation from the United States. The move comes shortly after Venezuelan opposition leader [[Juan Guaidó]] met with U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] at the [[White House]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-politics-usa-citgo/u-s-condemns-detention-of-citgo-executives-in-venezuela-hints-at-sanctions-on-russia-idUSKBN2002WD (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Algerian President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] pardons a further 6,000 prisoners after doing the same to another 3,000 two days ago. The mass pardons this week follow an offer of dialogue with the protesters, the release of detainees arrested at demonstrations, the formation of a committee to amend the constitution and meetings with opposition figures. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-algeria-pardon/algerian-leader-pardons-more-than-6000-prisoners-in-conciliatory-gesture-idUSKBN2001OX (Reuters)]
*A man is charged with [[rape in India|raping]] a five-year-old girl inside of the [[Embassy of the United States, New Delhi|United States embassy]] in [[New Delhi]]. The high-security mansion in the Indian capital is one of the most secure in [[Delhi]], with multiple layers of manned and electronic security. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/06/man-charged-rape-girl-5-us-embassy-complex-delhi (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Minister president (Germany)|Minister-President]] of the central [[States of Germany|German state]] of [[Thuringia]], [[Thomas Kemmerich]], resigns under national pressure after his controversial election to the position with the help of the [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|far-right]] party [[Alternative for Germany]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51399445 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Christina Koch]] returns to [[Earth]] from the [[International Space Station]] after a continuous 328 days in space, longer than any woman in history. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/technology/astronaut-christina-koch-lands-back-on-earth-after-a-record-breaking-328-days-in-space/ar-BBZGO30?OCID=ansmsnnews11 (CNN via MSN)]
